correctness.rationale: The repaired finding is exactly the classification of S=78 and S=77, with the known sorted bound and shift profiles cited as background. The edge definition matches repeated integer convexification because consecutive image segments overlap at their endpoints and together cover the whole image hull. Thus the first return is a shortest positive closed walk, which exists by the return of the original sites at step 13 and has a simple shortest representative of length at most 12. The frozen C++ builds precisely these edge masks and checks for return before discarding already expanded vertices, which cannot shorten a first return incorrectly. Rooting an orbit at 0 gives unique fixed-successor blocks of 11! suffixes. The independent checker uses factoradic unranking and queries the min and max of every image interval from two overlapping power-of-two ranges; it records first containment directly, without any graph search. Its twelve completed blocks certify 479001600 cycles, zero missing returns, zero inequality violations, 12 sum-78 translations and no other sum-78 cycles, precisely two sum-77 nontranslations, and 479001586 below 77. The two witness lists and their common profile (1,2,3,4,5,6,6,8,9,10,11,12) agree with the repaired text. The proof is a complete finite census for thirteen sites, not a classification of rigidity for all n.

value.rationale: Once the all-order bound is known, its equality and first stability tier are natural structural questions about the same adjacent-return statistic. At thirteen sites the census distinguishes having twelve known extremizers from knowing that none others exist, and shows that there are only two first-deficit patterns with a single shared characteristic profile. The exact witnesses and rigidity supply benchmarks for any general characterization. The finite contribution is not credited merely for rechecking the universal bound, the number of cycles traversed, or a conjecture frontier.
